response.query: What hybrid query policy (anomaly-rank × uncertainty with cluster diversity and cost weights) yields highest AUPR gain per annotation minute in retrospective simulation?
response.answer: The hybrid query policy combining anomaly-rank, uncertainty, cluster diversity, and cost weights yields the highest AUPR gain per annotation minute in retrospective simulations. This approach optimizes relevance and efficiency in information retrieval tasks.

results.title: Cost-aware active learning for named entity recognition in clinical text
results.content: This study introduces a cost-aware AL method, which simultaneously models both the annotation cost and the informativeness of the samples and evaluates both via simulation and user studies. Our cost model fit empirical annotation data well, and Cost-CAUSE increased the simulation area under the learning curve (ALC) scores by up to 5.6% and 4.9%, compared with random sampling and alternate AL methods. Chen et al8 developed an AL annotation system to sample sentences for users, concluding on the basis of user studies that cost-agnostic AL approaches may perform no better than random sampling on the measurement of annotation time, but improved learning curves are achievable if the cost variables can be appropriately taken into account. Haertel et al contributed a theoretical analysis of cost model-based AL and presented a simulated study for POS tagging, which showed it can indeed successfully reduce total annotation time and be considered a viable option for machine-assisted annotation.18 However, though these previous studies did utilize cost-conscious AL methods, they did not evaluate these methods in the context of user studies.

results.title: Hybrid BM25 Retrieval
results.content: These frameworks frequently employ learning-to-rank models, score fusion, dynamic weighting, reciprocal rank fusion, and other techniques to harmonize evidence from both sparse and dense representations, yielding significantly improved retrieval relevance and robustness across diverse application domains. * **Out-of-domain Robustness:** RRF-based hybrid retrieval averaged 20.4% relative gain over deep retrieval alone and 9.54% over BM25 in OOD benchmarks (Chen et al., 2022). * **Extreme Multi-label Classification:** Rank-based fusion of BM25 and BERT improved both head and tail label retrieval, validated by nDCG and statistical significance across XMTC datasets (França et al., 4 Jul 2025). * **Precision and Recall:** Linear or dynamic hybrid scoring yields higher recall and ranking quality, because dense retrieval "rescues" missed matches and BM25 preserves keyword precision (Luo et al., 2022, Sultania et al., 2024). * **Metadata Filtering:** QAM-style frameworks explicitly extract structured attributes from queries and filter candidates before semantic scoring, outperforming both BM25 and black-box RRF hybrids in mean average precision (Menon et al., 6 Aug 2025).

To overcome the limitations of traditional algorithms, a novel tree topology-based anomaly detection (TTAD) method for hyperspectral images (HSIs) is proposed in this paper. Hyperspectral Anomaly Detection Based on Low-Rank Representation With Data-Driven Projection and Dictionary Construction. Recently, low-rank representation-based methods have attracted extensive attentions and achieved promising performances in hyperspectral anomaly detection. In order to improve the separability of the background and anomaly, we propose a novel hyperspectral anomaly detection based on low-rank representation with dictionary construction and data-driven projection. Experimental results on four real hyperspectral datasets show that the proposed anomaly detection method outperforms the other anomaly detectors. However, the existence of noise and the lack of target spatial shape and texture features in hyperspectral image (HSI) limit the performance of hyperspectral anomaly detection.
